thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty page fired (PGD-4821) — high error rate: TLS handshake failures at edge -> upstream LB targets failing health checks. Affected region: us-east-1. Escalation policy: infra-oncall -> infra-lead. Root ts: 1984523123

pagerduty: Incident PGD-4821 triggered by metric rule 'edge_tls_handshake_rate' (threshold: >0.8% for 2m). Notified: #incidents, oncall@mredwood.io

mike: acked (mike) 1m — grabbing context. Seeing spike in SYN/TLS errors at edge.

mike: quick check: LB target health shows 40% unhealthy across gce-backend-us-east-1a and us-east-1b. DNS looks normal but TTLs are low (60s) — could be propagation thrash.

priya: oncall takeover in 10min FYI (end of shift) — if we need long-running work, i'll handoff.

sam: joining — any customer-facing impact yet? status page?

mike: early impact: small percentage of API requests 502/524, mostly requests hitting long-lived connections that fail TLS handshake. Some customers in east seeing transient errors. Not full outage.

ashley: stacktrace from edge logs (sanitized):
```
2026-03-14T21:02:10Z edge01 tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate
2026-03-14T21:02:11Z lb-proxy upstream: health_check failed: 502
2026-03-14T21:02:12Z edge01 tls: handshake timeout
```

juan: I see a recent cert rotation job completed 7m ago for edge cert bundle — could be related. Filing quick check: `kubectl get jobs -n certs` shows cert-rotator-20260314 completed at 20:56Z.

mike: good catch — rolling back certs is invasive. Let's confirm whether the LB TLS config changed.

ops-bot: Querying LB health: us-east-1a: 42% unhealthy, us-east-1b: 39% unhealthy, us-west-2: 1% unhealthy. Active connections dropped ~35% in us-east.

sam: mitigation plan options: 1) remove unhealthy targets from LB and let traffic drain to healthy region, 2) roll back recent cert bundle, 3) temporarily route traffic away from us-east via DNS failover (may be TTL-limited).

priya: i'm going to attempt targeted removal of suspected bad targets (us-east backend group) to stop churn and let healthy nodes serve. Will coordinate with networking.

mike: confirm might cause 1-2s extra latency while routes converge, but should reduce handshake errors.

priya: running command to mark targets unhealthy (AWS CLI snippet):
```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes 
  --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:tg/us-east-svc 
  --attributes Key=stickiness.enabled,Value=false
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:... --targets Id=i-0abcde1f2
```

(reacts :white_check_mark:) priya: removed 4 suspect instances from us-east target group, waiting 30s for health to stabilize.

incident-bot: Note: automatic retry policy in route-mapper triggered failover to secondary region for flows that exceeded handshake timeout; change recorded.

mike: checking error rates... they dropped from 1.2% -> 0.18% after the removals. Good signal.

ashley: can someone verify cert chain on one removed instance? grabbed a debug copy:
```
openssl s_client -connect edge01.redwood:443 -showcerts
# output: cert CN=*.redwood-inference.com, issuer=ACME CA v2, cert chain ok, but intermediate missing in chain on some nodes
```

juan: intermediate missing on two nodes — consistent with cert-rotator job not bundling the intermediate. That would explain 'bad certificate' handshake errors while some nodes serve new combined bundle.

sam: verdict: root cause likely faulty cert rotation that omitted intermediate certificate on a subset of nodes, causing TLS handshake failures -> LB target health flapping -> increased errors and DNS-based failover churn.

mike: action items immediate: (1) keep bad nodes out of pool (priya), (2) trigger cert re-deploy with full chain and verify on all nodes (juan + ashley), (3) monitor error rates & SLOs (mike), (4) update status page message if customer impact increases (sam).

priya: handing off to priya@shift — my shift ends in 6m, i'll stay until certs are redeployed and error rate stable. Handoff note: dropped targets remain out; need to register back after verifying proper chain.

sam: i'm publishing an internal incident note: "Partial TLS failures in us-east due to incomplete cert chain on rotated nodes. Mitigation: removed bad nodes, redeploy cert with full chain, monitoring. No large-scale customer outage; some east-region degraded errors." Will publish status page update if errors >1% for 5m.

mike: ack. I put a short runbook snippet in the incident doc:
- Check cert-rotator job logs: `kubectl logs job/cert-rotator-YYYY -n certs`
- Verify cert chain: `openssl s_client -connect <host>:443 -showcerts`
- If missing intermediate, re-run rotator with `--include-intermediate` flag and redeploy

ashley: re-deploy started (juan + ashley). Patching image with fixed rotator 1.2.3 -> job triggered at 21:10Z.

incident-bot: PagerDuty PGD-4821 acknowledged by mike at 1984523126. Escalation canceled.

priya: error rate steady at 0.14% now. LB health shows us-east unhealthy down to 5% after removals. Will keep monitoring for 10 more minutes before reinserting nodes.

mike: plan to re-register nodes one-by-one after confirming full chain and stable health checks. Start with canary node in us-east-1a.

juan: cert re-issue completed, verified full chain on canary node. Health check passed. Re-registering canary back into target group.

priya: canary healthy for 3m. Re-inserting remaining nodes gradually (2 at a time) with 30s pause.

ashley: all nodes in us-east re-registered by 21:21Z, health stable. Error rate at 0.06%.

sam: status: mitigated. Customer impact: low / intermittent errors for <30m. Postmortem owner: sam. Severity: Sev3.

mike: handoff notes for next oncall: monitor TLS handshake metric and LB target flaps; verify cert-rotator integration tests include intermediate bundling.

priya: i'll follow up with certs team to add CI check and an alert if cert chain validation fails during rotation.

juan: filing follow-up ticket: INFRA-9482 (add intermediate test + rollback guard).

sam: thanks all. Closing Slack thread once we confirm no regressions for 1h. Leaving a link to incident doc: https://redwood-internal/incident/PGD-4821 (internal)

mike: one last note: PagerDuty auto-notify window suppressed after ack; re-open if errors resurface. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident PGD-4821 status -> mitigated. Closed at 1984523903.
